# Copilot instructions for happy-home

## Repository overview

This is a household recurring-task manager built as a Next.js app with a Convex backend and a browser service worker for push notifications. The app is centered around recurring chores/tasks with assignees, visibility rules, due dates, and notification logic.

## Commands

Use the project scripts from the root package.json:

```bash
npm run dev          # Start the Next.js app (webpack build, not Turbopack)
npx convex dev      # Start the local Convex backend
npm run build        # Build the service worker and the Next.js app
npm run build:sw     # Build the service worker only
npm run typecheck    # Type-check the main app
npm run typecheck-sw # Type-check the service worker config
npm run lint        # Lint with oxlint
npm run knip         # Check for unused exports/files
npm run test         # Full static validation: typecheck + typecheck-sw + lint + knip
```

There is no Jest/Vitest test suite in this repo. For targeted validation on a changed area, prefer the project-level static checks:

```bash
npx oxlint src/app/Main.tsx
npx oxlint src/convex/tasks.ts
npx tsgo -p tsconfig.json
npx tsgo -p src/service-worker/tsconfig.json
```

If you need a single-file validation without touching unrelated code, run the file-specific linter or the relevant project typecheck command instead of the full suite.

## Architecture

- Frontend: `src/app/` and `src/components/` are the Next.js App Router UI. The main view is a task dashboard that groups tasks by status (`À faire`, `En attente`, `Corbeille`) and relies on URL state from `nuqs` for search/edit state.
- Data model: the core task logic lives in `src/shared/tasks.ts` and `src/shared/units.ts`. This is where status calculation, time conversions, sorting, and notification thresholds are defined.
- Convex backend: `src/convex/` contains queries/mutations for tasks, users, accomplishments, auth, subscriptions, and notification dispatch. `parseTask()` in `src/convex/tasks.ts` converts raw `Doc<"tasks">` objects into the richer `Task` shape and enforces `visibleTo` visibility rules.
- Auth and PWA notifications: auth is integrated with `@convex-dev/auth`; push notifications are sent via `web-push` and are handled by the service worker under `src/service-worker/`.
- Shared types and utilities: `src/shared/` is shared between frontend and backend and should be the first place to look for task semantics and time behavior.
- Generated Convex files: do not edit `src/convex/_generated/**`; it is generated by Convex.

## Key conventions

- Use the `@/*` alias for imports from `src/*`.
- Use vanilla-extract (`*.css.ts`) for styling. Do not introduce plain CSS, CSS modules, or Tailwind classes.
- UI copy is in French; preserve that language in components and messages unless the change is truly technical/internal.
- Task semantics are intentionally centralized in `src/shared/tasks.ts`. If a bug affects `dueSoon`, `dueNow`, sorting, `isTaskFailed`, or notification timing, fix it there and check the call sites that consume it.
- Convex queries filter using `visibleTo`; do not assume all tasks are visible to every user.
- Authenticated queries are typically gated with `getAuthUserId(ctx)` and return empty arrays or `undefined` when the user is not logged in.
- When working on Convex code, read `src/convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` first. It contains repository-specific Convex guidance that overrides generic advice.
- Environment variables for deployment are expected to be present in the app/runtime environment. The app relies on Convex URL configuration and VAPID data for push notifications.

## Useful repository-specific notes

- The main app is a single-page task dashboard, not a multi-page CRUD app.
- The app uses client-side task urgency sorting and timer-based refreshes (`useTimestamp`) to update due state over time.
- Notification scheduling is not ad hoc; it is tied to the task model and `shouldNotifyForTask()` logic in `src/shared/tasks.ts`.
- The service worker is compiled separately from the app (`build:sw`) and emitted to `public/sw.js`.

## Existing AI instructions incorporated

This repo already contains Convex-specific guidance in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, and the project currently asks agents to read `src/convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` before editing Convex code. Keep that requirement in place when working on backend logic.
